title: Phantom Blade Zero PC Requirements - What Is Confirmed
description: System requirements for Phantom Blade Zero on PC have not been published. Here is what is confirmed - Unreal Engine 5, native DLSS 4.5, ray-traced reflections - and how to judge your hardware before the October 29 release.

facts.label: System requirements
facts.value: Published alongside the October 2026 preview coverage

facts.label: Path tracing
facts.value: Supported on PC, on top of ray-traced reflections and shadows

facts.label: Review performance
facts.value: Split: Screen Rant says PC 'barely ever skips a frame'; Combo Infinito lists PC performance as a flaw - neither published specs or frame-time data

sections.title: The Requirements Are Not Out Yet
sections.content:
S-GAME has not published minimum or recommended PC specifications. Any table you see listing a specific GPU, CPU or RAM requirement before launch is either copied from another Unreal Engine 5 game or guessed.

That includes this page - so instead of inventing numbers, this page records what is actually confirmed and what those facts imply about your hardware.

sections.title: What Is Confirmed
sections.content:
FeatureStatusWhat it means for hardware
Unreal Engine 5ConfirmedBaseline VRAM and CPU demand of a current-gen UE5 title
Native DLSS 4.5ConfirmedNVIDIA cards get frame generation and upscaling from day one
Ray-traced reflectionsConfirmedThe most expensive feature; expect a large performance gap on/off
Ray-traced shadowsConfirmedSecond-largest cost; likely a separate toggle
Steam Deck / handheldNot addressedNo statement yet
FSR / XeSS supportNot announcedDLSS being native does not confirm AMD or Intel upscaling

sections.title: What You Can Reasonably Expect
sections.content:
Reasoned inference, clearly labelled as such - not a spec sheet:

  • VRAM will be the limiting factor. A UE5 game with ray-traced reflections and shadows on a large, dense world is not going to be comfortable at 8GB. Modern AAA titles with similar features commonly ask for more.
  • DLSS 4.5 being native is good news for NVIDIA owners. Frame generation should carry a mid-range card much further than raw rasterisation would.
  • AMD and Intel owners should wait for the requirements post. DLSS being announced natively says nothing about FSR or XeSS, and there is no confirmation either way.
  • Ray tracing will be the settings switch, not the CPU. If you need headroom, turn reflections down before you consider the hardware inadequate.

sections.title: When the Real Numbers Arrive
sections.content:
Requirements are normally published by the publisher in the weeks before release, on the Steam store page and the official site. With an October 29, 2026 launch, expect them during October.

Two reliable signals that they are out: the Steam store page gaining a System Requirements section, and an official post from S-GAME or the game's channels. Until then, treat every number as unconfirmed.

sections.title: Related
sections.content: The release date page tracks the schedule. If you are deciding whether to pre-order while waiting for the specs, the pre-order guide explains what you do and do not gain by committing early - the short version is that the announced bonuses are both obtainable in-game.

sections.title: What changed this week
sections.content:
Two PC details arrived with the October preview round: the game ships with Denuvo anti-tamper, and it supports path tracing in addition to the ray-traced reflections already listed. Official system requirements were published alongside that coverage.

A caution worth carrying into launch week: one preview team reported rare but extreme frame-rate drops even on a high-end PC, and the preview build was PC-only, so PlayStation 5 performance has not been independently seen.

sections.title: What The Reviews Say About Performance
sections.content:
Reviews lifted 25-26 October 2026 and the performance picture got closer, not settled:

  • Screen Rant (9/10) reports PC performance that "barely ever skips a frame". That is one reviewer on one machine, with no hardware list and no frame-time capture published alongside it.
  • Combo Infinito (95) names PC performance as one of the things keeping the game from perfection.
  • Critical Hits, in the review that leaked before the embargo and was deleted, described smooth visuals in Balanced mode on a base PS5 - PlayStation hardware, not PC.
  • The October previews had flagged unstable frame rates during heavy combat, which is part of why the release was pushed from 9 September.

Two things are missing and you should hold the page to them: measured frame-pacing data, and any testing of the Denuvo anti-tamper that ships on the PC release. For a game whose parry windows are its core skill check, average FPS is the wrong statistic - frame-time consistency is the one that matters, and nobody has published it yet. Digital Foundry-style breakdowns normally land on or after the launch date, so check back.

Meanwhile the published requirements stand: Windows 10/11 64-bit, 16 GB RAM, an SSD install (roughly 135 GB, see release date), with the GTX 1660 6 GB / RX 5500 XT 8 GB minimum tier targeting 1080p30 with upscaling rather than without it. Read the minimum line as an upscaling-assisted target.
